[[File:Cavalier Hotel Virginia Beach postcard.jpg|thumb|right|260px|The Cavalier Hotel, Virginia Beach.]]
[[File:Cavalier Hotel Virginia Beach 2019.jpg|thumb|right|260px|The Cavalier Hotel, 2019. Photo: Carol M. Highsmith.]]
'''1998 Decipher World Championship''' was the third Star Wars CCG World Championship. Play was Saturday 21 and Sunday 22 November at the Cavalier Hotel, Virginia Beach, Virginia.<ref name="pkt">[https://blog.categoryonegames.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/1998-World-Championship.pdf 1998 World Championship packet], Decipher / Kendrick Summers (20 November 1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195330/https://blog.categoryonegames.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/1998-World-Championship.pdf Internet Archive].</ref> Decipher's packet is dated 20 November 1998 over [[Kendrick Summers]]' letterhead. The field was 56 finalists, including more than ten players from earlier World Finals.<ref name="pkt" /><ref name="insider43">Ryan Morris, "The Thrill of Victory", ''Star Wars Insider'' #43, pp. 64–65. Scan: [https://archive.org/details/starwarsinsider_1_to_153_plus_specials Star Wars Insider Magazines (1 to 153 + Specials)], Internet Archive. Facebook photographs, Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016012404/https://swccg.com/snapshots/facebook/insider-1998-worlds-p64.html Internet Archive] (p. 64); [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016012452/https://swccg.com/snapshots/facebook/insider-1998-worlds-p65.html Internet Archive] (p. 65)</ref>

This was the first constructed Worlds to use [[Special Edition]] before the public street date. Each finalist received a complete set of the expansion to build from.<ref name="insider43" /> [[Trandosite]] later called the weekend the Operative Worlds.<ref name="trando">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050517110350/http://trandosite.mcmail.com/wf00p2.htm History of the World Finals], [[Trandosite]].</ref>

[[Matt Potter]] of Duluth, Minnesota, defeated [[Michael Riboulet]] (United Kingdom) 2 (+9) and became the first American World Champion.<ref name="insider43" /><ref name="trando" /> Riboulet became the first player in two Grand Finals.<ref name="trando" /> Potter qualified through Bespin St. Charles; Riboulet through Kiffex Euro GenCon from Bristol.<ref name="pkt" />

The grand prize was an all-expense paid trip and VIP pass to Star Wars Celebration in Denver, 30 April–2 May 1999. The site was the Wings Over the Rockies Air and Space Museum.<ref name="insider43" /> [[Philipp Jacobs]], the 1997 World Champion, received a special invitation and did not have to qualify.<ref name="insider43" /><ref name="pkt" />

== Operatives ==

Matching [[Operatives]] with [[Imperial Occupation / Imperial Control]] and [[Local Uprising / Liberation]] defined the weekend.<ref name="trando" /><ref name="insider43" /> On Saturday [[Tomoya Suzuki]] led the field, with [[Lucas Hernandez]] just behind. [[Evan Ferguson]] finished 14th, the highest finisher who did not play Operatives. [[Philipp Jacobs]] just missed the twelve; Riboulet made it.<ref name="trando" />

On Sunday the twelve restarted at 0. Hernandez of Oregon led the remaining four with three wins. He played Riboulet for a place in the two-game final; Potter played [[Stuart Jones]] of Australia for the other place. The finalists were Potter and Riboulet.<ref name="insider43" /><ref name="trando" />

Riboulet won the first game of the final by 19 with Dark Operatives. Potter won the second by 28, also on Operatives, retrieving a large amount of cards in the last seconds. Potter won 2 (+9).<ref name="trando" /><ref name="insider43" />

Potter's day-one Dark list is 20 [[Eriadu Operative]] under Imperial Occupation. His Light list is 20 [[Alderaan Operative]] under Local Uprising.<ref name="trando" />

After the event Decipher issued errata that hit [[Spaceport Speeders]] ([[Jon VanDerMeer]]'s timeout Light), then Operatives, [[Floating Refinery]], and [[Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers|Hidden Base]].<ref name="trando" /> Trandosite wrote that 1998 created more errata than Decipher had given out before.<ref name="trando" />

Friday night's banquet in the Cavalier showed the Episode I trailer, released to the public a few days earlier. Saturday play used 28 tables with country flags, news computers, and web cameras. After the final, [[Carol Wisely]], Decipher's Vice-President of Marketing, awarded medals as John Williams music played, and [[Warren Holland]] shook hands.<ref name="insider43" />

== Format ==

* '''Environment:''' [[Premiere - Special Edition]]
* '''Site:''' Cavalier Hotel, Virginia Beach, Virginia
* '''Field:''' 56 finalists<ref name="pkt" />

Packet structure (see [[Tournaments#1998 World Championship packet]]): Saturday Swiss, 4 rounds / eight games, top twelve advance. Those twelve may change decks Saturday night only. Sunday the twelve restart at 0 for four 60-minute games; top two play a two-game final. Everyone outside the twelve plays Sunday sealed. Highest total from Sunday's four games set allegiance for the first game of the final. Players handed in a deck list Saturday morning before play, and again Sunday morning if they reached the twelve. Players were to be prepared by 7:45am.<ref name="pkt" />

== Schedule ==

Friday 20 November: finalists check into the Cavalier 1:00am–6:00pm; reception 6:30–8:30pm in Ballroom C; Q&A 8:30–10:00pm in Ballroom B. Saturday 21 November: breakfast 6:30–8:30am; preliminary tournament 8:00am–6:00pm in Ballroom A; lunch buffet 12:00–2:00pm; banquet 7:00–10:00pm in Orion's Lounge (11th floor). Sunday 22 November: breakfast 6:30–8:30am; finals 8:00am–3:00pm in Ballroom A; sealed deck 8:00am–1:00pm in Ballroom B; lunch buffet 12:00–2:00pm; awards 3:15–3:45pm; departure 4:00pm.<ref name="pkt" />
